name: Radio Group
description: A set of checkable buttons where no more than one can be checked at a time, with keyboard navigation that moves focus and selection together.

keyboard_interactions.action: Moves focus into the group on checked button, or first button if none checked
Checks the focused radio button if not already checked
Moves focus and checks next button; wraps from last to first
Moves focus and checks next button; wraps from last to first
Moves focus and checks previous button; wraps from first to last
Moves focus and checks previous button; wraps from first to last

required_attributes.description: true when checked; false when unchecked

notes: Use native <input type='radio'> with a shared `name`. The browser gives you the roving tabindex, the arrow keys, the wrapping, and the mutual exclusion — all the hard parts.

A radio GROUP is one Tab stop. Tab enters on the checked option (or the first if none is checked); arrows move within. This is native behaviour you get free, and the first thing lost when you build it from divs.
fieldset + legend is mandatory (RAWeb 11.5). The legend is the question; the labels are the answers.
Radios cannot be unchecked by the user. If 'none' is a valid answer, provide an explicit 'None' option — or use checkboxes.
Never put a radio group in a fieldset with no legend: a fieldset alone gives a border, not a name.
role='radiogroup' + role='radio' is only for cases where a native input truly cannot work. You then owe the arrows, the roving tabindex, and the exclusion logic yourself.

raweb_criteria.reason: Each radio is a form field and needs its own label.
THE criterion for this pattern. A radio group without fieldset/legend announces the options but never the question they answer.
Each option's label must be meaningful on its own — announced out of context, 'Option 1' means nothing.
Arrow keys must move between options; the group must be one Tab stop.
The focus ring must be visible, including on custom-styled radios.
